items.question: What practice must be maintained after worshipping this circle?
premises: The application continues for a duration
items.inference: After worshipping this circle, one should continue applying meditation for as long as the practice lasts.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped this circle, one should apply meditation for as long as one continues the practice.

items.question: What kinds of languages become perceptible during this meditative state?
items.inference: During this state, diverse languages, both previously heard and unheard, become perceptible.
items.plain_english: Indeed, languages of various forms, both unheard and heard before, arise.

items.question: How and where are these languages heard by the practitioner?
premises: The practitioner is both agent and recipient
The hearing takes place within oneself
items.inference: The languages are heard spontaneously by oneself, to oneself, and within oneself.
items.plain_english: They are heard spontaneously by oneself, to oneself, and within oneself.

items.question: What physical transformation results from this yogic accomplishment?
premises: The practitioner becomes free of wrinkles and grey hair
The resemblance is that of a second Kāma
items.inference: The practitioner becomes rejuvenated and appears like a second god of love.
items.plain_english: Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, he becomes like a second god of love.

rows.grounds: source or force to be destroyed

items.question: What effect on speech can be produced through this practice?
premises: A force such as wind is to be destroyed by speech
The practitioner remains like a mute
items.inference: By this practice one can destroy forces like wind through speech, causing one to remain as if mute.
uncertainties: The exact referent of vāyvādeḥ and the mechanism of nāśayet are contextually ambiguous.
items.plain_english: One should destroy the force of wind and so forth by speech; indeed, he then remains like a mute.

items.question: What is the supreme function of the seventh circle?
premises: The seventh circle is addressed to the goddess
It has the power to paralyze armies
items.inference: The seventh circle is supreme and has the power to paralyze armies.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the seventh circle is supreme and causes the paralysis of armies.

items.question: What perceptual ability arises for one devoted to worship and meditation in that circle?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to worship and meditation
items.inference: One devoted to worship and meditation in that circle gains vision from afar.
items.plain_english: And for one devoted to worship and meditation in that circle, vision arises from afar.

items.question: What additional magical powers are associated with this practice?
premises: Paralyzing, deluding, and similar powers are mentioned
These are addressed to the beloved
items.inference: The practice grants powers such as killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and the like.
items.plain_english: O fortunate one, O beloved, killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and so forth are achieved.

items.question: What condition is necessary for success in this method?
premises: The method of eight times eight must be known
items.inference: One succeeds only by knowing the eight-times-eight method, and not otherwise.
items.plain_english: Indeed, having known the method of the eight groups of eight, one succeeds, and not otherwise.

items.question: How should the teaching be ascertained according to the speaker?
premises: The speaker has declared it without doubt
Devotion and reasoning are the means
items.inference: The teaching, declared without doubt, should be ascertained through devotion and reasoning.
items.plain_english: Indeed, I have declared this without doubt; it should be ascertained with devotion and reasoning.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
items.inference: This is the eighth chapter in the work emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: The eighth chapter in the work emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: What topic does the speaker promise to explain to the beloved?
premises: The speaker promises to tell something
The topic is the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs
items.inference: The speaker promises to explain the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs to the beloved.
items.plain_english: O beloved, I shall tell you the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.

items.question: What collective domain encompasses all earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs?
premises: They belong to a complete field-group
items.inference: All earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs belong to the complete field-group.
uncertainties: The precise technical meaning of sarvakṣetrakam is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: The complete field-group of all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.

items.question: Which categories of yoginīs are enumerated in this grouping?
items.inference: The grouping includes all innate, all family-born, and all door-guardian yoginīs.
items.plain_english: All the innate ones, all those born of the families, and all the door-guardians.

items.question: Why has the supreme secret among secrets been revealed?
premises: It is the supreme secret among secrets
The revelation is due to devotion
items.inference: The supreme secret among secrets has been revealed because of your devotion.
items.plain_english: The supreme secret of secrets has been revealed because of your devotion.

items.question: What teaching does the speaker now wish to hear from the gurus?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The wish is to hear from the gurus
The topic is the worship of the siddhas
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear about the worship of the siddhas from the gurus.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.

items.question: What should be given to others according to this instruction?
premises: An arrangement of two syllables is specified
items.inference: One should give the arrangement of two syllables to others.
uncertainties: The identity of 'others' (anyanteṣu) is not fully specified.
items.plain_english: One should give the arrangement of the two syllables to others.

items.question: How does this knowledge compare to any future knowledge?
premises: This knowledge is taken as the standard
No equal knowledge will arise again
items.inference: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there ever be again.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there ever be again.

items.question: What does the speaker promise to explain to the beautiful-eyed one?
premises: The speaker addresses the beautiful-eyed one
The topic is the method of their names
items.inference: The speaker promises to explain the method of their names to the beautiful-eyed one.
uncertainties: The referent of 'them' (teṣāṃ) depends on prior context.
items.plain_english: O beautiful-eyed one, listen; I shall speak the method of their names.

items.question: Who are identified as the independent impellers of the family across the four ages?
premises: They are impellers of the family
items.inference: The independent impellers of the family are identified in relation to the four ages.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of caturyuga iti is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: O Lord, thus are the independent impellers of the family in the four ages.

items.question: What is the extent and origin of this Kaula teaching?
premises: This Kaula teaching is the subject
items.inference: This Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, extends to ten crores in measure.
uncertainties: The exact meaning of daśakoṭipramāṇaṃ (verses, mantras, or beings) is unclear.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, is ten crores in measure.

items.question: By what agency and will does the yoginī named Icchā operate up to the limit of māyā?
premises: The operation extends up to māyā by supreme will
items.inference: The yoginī named Icchā, through the siddhas and by supreme will, operates up to the limit of māyā.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation between siddhaiḥ and the rest of the clause is compressed.
items.plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, with the siddhas, extends up to māyā by supreme will.

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching concerning the mothers in this lineage?
premises: The mothers are the subject group
items.inference: The teaching concerning the mothers was told again by the sky-movers.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, O beloved, it was told again to the mothers by the sky-movers.

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching to the earth-moving yoginīs who are good eaters?
premises: The recipients are the earth-moving yoginīs

items.inference: The teaching was told to the earth-moving, good-eating yoginīs by an earth-mover.
